title: Universal Commerce Protocol — homepage
quote: Three launch capabilities: Checkout, Identity Linking, Order Management. Compatible with AP2, A2A, MCP. Co-developers: Google, Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart. Endorsed by 30+ organizations. Licensed under Apache 2.0.

title: Under the Hood: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) — Google Developers Blog
quote: Businesses publish capabilities via /.well-known/ucp containing service definitions, capability listings with schemas and extension relationships, and payment handler configurations. UCP separates payment instruments (what consumers use) from handlers (payment processors). Reference handlers: Shop Pay, Google Pay, mock. Transports: REST, MCP, A2A.

title: Google Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) Guide
quote: Native Checkout integrates checkout logic directly with AI Mode in Google Search and Gemini. Embedded Checkout is an iframe-based option for bespoke flows. Implementation supports REST API and MCP binding. Merchants remain the Merchant of Record.

title: universal-commerce-protocol/ucp — GitHub spec repository
quote: Initial capabilities: Checkout, Identity Linking, Order, Payment Token Exchange. Full spec at ucp.dev/specification/overview. SDK repositories under the Universal-Commerce-Protocol organization.

title: Secure Agent Commerce with AP2 and UCP — Google Codelabs
quote: Five core tools: discover_theaters, search_movies, get_movie_detail, create_checkout, complete_purchase. CartMandate: merchant-signed price guarantee locked at checkout (10-minute expiration window). PaymentMandate: user-authorized charge referencing the CartMandate. Double signature verification. require_confirmation=True wrapper pauses complete_purchase. Production would use SD-JWT-VC signatures replacing SHA-256 hashes; official wallet SDK for user consent.

title: Building the Universal Commerce Protocol (2026) — Shopify Engineering
quote: Decentralized extensibility: merchants define custom extensions using reverse-domain naming without central approval. Capability negotiation: both agents and merchants publish profiles; the merchant computes their intersection at request time. Dynamic payment negotiation: handlers vary based on cart, location, and transaction details.

title: UCP FAQ — Google for Developers
quote: AP2 (Agent Payments Protocol) serves as a specialized payment processing layer within UCP's broader architecture. We use UCP to orchestrate the broader purchase lifecycle, while AP2 can be used as a specialized payment layer within UCP. Merchants don't require Google Pay API integration on their properties — only PSP token processing capability.

title: New tech and tools for retailers to succeed in an agentic shopping era — Google Blog
quote: Universal Commerce Protocol launched as a new open standard. Co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, Walmart. Endorsed by 20+ companies including Stripe, Adyen, Visa, Mastercard, Best Buy, Macy's, The Home Depot, Flipkart, Zalando. Business Agent went live January 12, 2026.

title: OpenAI's ACP and Google's UCP: What's the Difference — Checkout.com
quote: ACP handles end-to-end commerce across AI assistants. UCP currently focuses narrowly on checkout and order-related flows. ACP uses single-use, time-bound, amount-restricted tokens; UCP integrates with Google Pay at launch with PayPal support planned. Merchants should prepare to support both.

title: Google Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP): Merchant Setup, Agentic Checkout & PPC Guide 2026 — ALM Corp
quote: Launched January 2026 at NRF. Merchant setup: add native_commerce: true attribute to eligible products in Merchant Center; verify PSP supports Google Pay tokens. UCP supports REST APIs, MCP, and A2A. Merchants remain sellers of record.

title: About UCP and UCP-powered checkout — Google Merchant Center Help
quote: Open standard for agentic commerce designed to work across the full shopping journey from discovery to post-purchase.

title: What is Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) — MetaRouter Blog
quote: Independent overview describing UCP's role for agents and merchants in the agentic commerce era.
